text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Important decisions to raise the standard of youth activities and sports in schools, sports centres and industries. Egypt to benefit from the sports capabilities of the armed forces and police.
- The President to witness the passage of Nile flood waters through the Toscha canal on October 15.
- Egypt reiterates its refusal of Israel's settlement policy and Assistant Foreign Minister Fathy el-Shazli says Israel's tone is disgusting.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri decrees banning public enterprises and ministries from buying any new furniture or fitting new telephone lines.

- U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry says Iraqi crisis diffusing. U.S. manoeuvres in Kuwait are continuing and the Carl Vinson is retreating. Baghdad says we have no designs on Kuwait and respect its border.
- Assistant Foreign Minister Fathy el-Shazli says Israel's latest statements contradict and obstruct peace efforts.
- Former German foreign minister Genscher lauds President Mubarak, says he is a strong character with an important role in the region.
- Prime minister Ganzouri chairs his first youth and sport council, pledges a spurt of sporting and youth related activities in a variety of fields.

- Minister of Public Works & Water Resources Abdel-Hadi Radi says Mubarak will witness the diversion of the Nile flood waters to irrigate 500,000 acres in the New Valley. Interior and Public Works ministries will form a committee to combat the danger of flash floods.
- Ganzouri decrees as head of the Youth and Sports Committee: school students to get a meal and sports will return to the school yard.
- Foreign Minister Moussa tells C.N.N.: the peace process is going through a hard time because the Palestinians and Israelis are not fulfilling their promises.
